- If sentiment is positive (≥ 0.5) in recent days, model tends to underreact — increase forecast slightly to avoid underestimating upward momentum.  
- If sentiment is negative (≤ -0.5) in recent days, model tends to overreact — decrease forecast slightly to avoid overestimating downward momentum.  
- Model consistently underestimates true price spikes — especially after sentiment shifts to positive; apply a 2–5% upward bias to forecast peak values.  
- Model overestimates early in the 30-day horizon when sentiment is neutral or negative — adjust downward by 1–3% for the first 5–7 days.  
- After a sharp price spike, model often overshoots and continues rising — apply a “mean reversion” correction: reduce forecast by 1–2% per day after peak until price stabilizes.  
- If sentiment history shows alternating +/– signals, model fails to capture volatility — use a “sentiment-weighted volatility buffer” to adjust forecast range ±1.5–2.5% around mean.  
- Model ignores sentiment-driven “reversal” signals — if sentiment flips from negative to positive within 3 days, reduce forecast slope by 10–20% for next 5 days.
